title: Backspace String Compare
statement:
# Backspace String Compare

Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if they are equal when both are typed into empty text editors where `'#'` represents a backspace character, or `false` otherwise.

When a backspace is typed, it removes the preceding non-backspace character if one is present. Backspacing over an empty text buffer leaves the buffer empty.

Constraints: `1 <= s.length <= 100` and `1 <= t.length <= 100`. Strings may contain alphanumeric characters and `'#'`.

examples.explanation: Both strings reduce to "ac": '#' deletes 'b' from s and 'd' from t.
s reduces to an empty string (two consecutive backspaces), while t stays "c".
Both reduce to "c": leading and mid-string '#'s cancel preceding characters, including the no-op leading '#'.

constraints: Function signature: `function backspaceCompare(s: string, t: string)`.
Inputs are JSON-serializable values satisfying the bounds stated above.
hints: Simulate typing: push regular characters and pop when you see '#'.
To save space, scan right-to-left and count how many '#' each backspace cancels.
Compare the rightmost surviving character of each string; advance both pointers only when they match.

editorial.approach: Process each string through a stack—push non-'#' characters, pop on '#'. The optimal variant scans both strings backward with two pointers and skip-counts, never materializing the reduced strings.
editorial.why_optimal: The stack approach runs O(n + m) time and O(n + m) space. The two-pointer scan keeps the same time bound but O(1) extra space. On the problem's 22 generated cases the optimal ran in 0.10 ms versus 0.31 ms for brute force—a ~3x gap.
editorial.pitfalls: A '#' at the start of a string must be a no-op; never pop past empty. Both pointers must fully consume their respective strings—do not return early on length mismatch alone.

solutions.title: Brute Force
solutions.complexity: Time: O(n + m) | Space: O(n + m)
